# 'A born astronaut': France's Sophie Adenot makes history with flight to space

 Science 

France's Sophie Adenot became only the second French woman to fly to space on Friday as her crew of four rocketed towards the International Space Station for an eight-month mission on board the orbiting laboratory, where a medical evacuation earlier this year left a skeleton crew of just three astronauts.

Issued on: 13/02/2026 - 12:47 Modified: 13/02/2026 - 16:38

 3 min Reading time

Share

 By: 

[FRANCE 24](https://www.france24.com/en/author/france-24/ "FRANCE 24")

![Image 1: Astronaut Sophie Adenot has become the second French woman to fly to space.](https://s.france24.com/media/display/c3088096-08d1-11f1-b2b8-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/c6fceb29daa8976102dace21b036bff9f3f6567a.jpg)

 Cover image: Sophie Adenot's journey to space fulfils a childhood dream. © Jim Watson, AFP 

11:38

When she was growing up, [Sophie Adenot](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/sophie-adenot/) plastered her childhood bedroom with posters of rockets launching from Cape Canaveral.

On Friday, she [blasted off](https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20260213-live-french-astronaut-sophie-adenot-set-for-launch-to-international-space-station-iss) from that very launchpad, fulfilling her childhood dream and becoming just the second French woman to fly to space.

Adenot is one of four astronauts now heading towards the [International Space Station](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/international-space-station/) to replace a crew that was evacuated last month because of an unidentified medical issue.

Read more[French astronaut Sophie Adenot blasts off to International Space Station](https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20260213-live-french-astronaut-sophie-adenot-set-for-launch-to-international-space-station-iss)

For the next eight months, the 43-year-old helicopter test pilot will conduct scientific experiments on the football field-sized station 400 kilometres above Earth.

Adenot has been dreaming of this moment since 1996, when she watched on television as France's first female astronaut Claudie Haigneré blasted off towards the Mir space station.

"I was 14 years old and it was a revelation," Adenot recently told a press conference.

![Image 2: Four astronauts blasts off towards the International Space Station](https://s.france24.com/media/display/c25fc01e-08d1-11f1-b36d-005056bfb2b6/w:980/39cf8c84d044a1878eeb8d542d890cba63862fa4.jpg)

 Four astronauts blasted off towards the International Space Station at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. © Jim Watson, AFP 

"At that moment, I told myself: one day, that will be me."

Haigneré told AFP that Adenot is both her "heir" and a "pioneer" in her own right.

"Sophie is a born astronaut," Haignere added.

After two days of delays, Adenot, [NASA](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/nasa/) astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway as well as Russian cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev launched on a [SpaceX](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/spacex/) Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral on Friday.

They are scheduled to arrive at the ISS on Saturday, where they will relieve a skeleton crew of three astronauts.

## Afghanistan rescue missions

As a teenager growing up in central France, Adenot cut space photos out of magazines and stuck them above her desk.

![Image 3: Adenot, right, with the other three astronauts launching to the ISS on Friday](https://s.france24.com/media/display/c1edea48-08d1-11f1-a48a-005056a90284/w:980/022241231c18c49406aac2d4f109445a53a1b08b.jpg)

 Adenot (right) with the other three astronauts who launched to the ISS on Friday. © Jim Watson, AFP file photo 

They were a source of motivation when she was studying maths, "which seemed so far removed from the space adventure I dreamt of", Adenot recently told a podcast.

She would go on to study at prestigious universities including MIT, and work at European aerospace giant Airbus as a helicopter cockpit designer.

Adenot credits her grandfather, a mechanic in France's air force, for giving her a love of "taking things apart and fixing them".

As a helicopter pilot, she completed two tours in Afghanistan, specialising in search and rescue missions.

Adenot then became France's first female helicopter test pilot in 2018.

"I love adventure, the unknown, facing improbable situations and seeing how we overcome them – whether as a team or alone," she said.

![Image 4: Adenot grew up dreaming of flying to space](https://s.france24.com/media/display/c17e7b2c-08d1-11f1-9031-005056a90284/w:980/49e6ffc47fb78e8ff11b6da2fcd875f435067f69.jpg)

 Adenot grew up dreaming of flying to space. © Pau Barrena, AFP file photo 

But while logging 3,000 flight hours and 120 combat missions, Adenot never stopped dreaming of space.

She first applied to be a [European Space Agency](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/european-space-agency/) astronaut in 2008 when she was just 25 – but was rejected.

However in 2022 she was selected out of 22,000 candidates, and embarked on three years of intense training to get ready for Friday's launch.

It has been a "tsunami" that has completely changed her life, the mother of a teenager has said.

## Michelin-starred cuisine

Adenot will be busy on board the orbiting scientific lab, participating in more than 200 experiments.

Research will include microgravity's effect on the human body, including measuring how her time in orbit impacts her memory.

She will also test a system that uses artificial intelligence and augmented reality to allow astronauts to carry out their own medical ultrasounds.

But it will not be all work.

French chef Anne-Sophie Pic, who has 10 Michelin stars, has prepared a menu for Adenot that includes lobster bisque and foie gras.

She has also recorded the sounds of birds singing, footsteps crunching on snow and flowing streams to remind her of life back on that blue planet she can see out of the window.

# 'A born astronaut': France's Sophie Adenot makes history with flight to space

 Science 

France's Sophie Adenot became only the second French woman to fly to space on Friday as her crew of four rocketed towards the International Space Station for an eight-month mission on board the orbiting laboratory, where a medical evacuation earlier this year left a skeleton crew of just three astronauts.

![Image 1: Astronaut Sophie Adenot has become the second French woman to fly to space.](https://s.france24.com/media/display/c3088096-08d1-11f1-b2b8-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/c6fceb29daa8976102dace21b036bff9f3f6567a.jpg)

11:38

When she was growing up, [Sophie Adenot](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/sophie-adenot/) plastered her childhood bedroom with posters of rockets launching from Cape Canaveral.

On Friday, she [blasted off](https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20260213-live-french-astronaut-sophie-adenot-set-for-launch-to-international-space-station-iss) from that very launchpad, fulfilling her childhood dream and becoming just the second French woman to fly to space.

Adenot is one of four astronauts now heading towards the [International Space Station](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/international-space-station/) to replace a crew that was evacuated last month because of an unidentified medical issue.

Read more[French astronaut Sophie Adenot blasts off to International Space Station](https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20260213-live-french-astronaut-sophie-adenot-set-for-launch-to-international-space-station-iss)

For the next eight months, the 43-year-old helicopter test pilot will conduct scientific experiments on the football field-sized station 400 kilometres above Earth.

Adenot has been dreaming of this moment since 1996, when she watched on television as France's first female astronaut Claudie Haigneré blasted off towards the Mir space station.

"I was 14 years old and it was a revelation," Adenot recently told a press conference.

![Image 2: Four astronauts blasts off towards the International Space Station](https://s.france24.com/media/display/c25fc01e-08d1-11f1-b36d-005056bfb2b6/w:980/39cf8c84d044a1878eeb8d542d890cba63862fa4.jpg)

 Four astronauts blasted off towards the International Space Station at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. © Jim Watson, AFP 

"At that moment, I told myself: one day, that will be me."

Haigneré told AFP that Adenot is both her "heir" and a "pioneer" in her own right.

"Sophie is a born astronaut," Haignere added.

After two days of delays, Adenot, [NASA](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/nasa/) astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway as well as Russian cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev launched on a [SpaceX](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/spacex/) Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral on Friday.

They are scheduled to arrive at the ISS on Saturday, where they will relieve a skeleton crew of three astronauts.

## Afghanistan rescue missions

As a teenager growing up in central France, Adenot cut space photos out of magazines and stuck them above her desk.

![Image 3: Adenot, right, with the other three astronauts launching to the ISS on Friday](https://s.france24.com/media/display/c1edea48-08d1-11f1-a48a-005056a90284/w:980/022241231c18c49406aac2d4f109445a53a1b08b.jpg)

 Adenot (right) with the other three astronauts who launched to the ISS on Friday. © Jim Watson, AFP file photo 

They were a source of motivation when she was studying maths, "which seemed so far removed from the space adventure I dreamt of", Adenot recently told a podcast.

She would go on to study at prestigious universities including MIT, and work at European aerospace giant Airbus as a helicopter cockpit designer.

Adenot credits her grandfather, a mechanic in France's air force, for giving her a love of "taking things apart and fixing them".

As a helicopter pilot, she completed two tours in Afghanistan, specialising in search and rescue missions.

Adenot then became France's first female helicopter test pilot in 2018.

"I love adventure, the unknown, facing improbable situations and seeing how we overcome them – whether as a team or alone," she said.

![Image 4: Adenot grew up dreaming of flying to space](https://s.france24.com/media/display/c17e7b2c-08d1-11f1-9031-005056a90284/w:980/49e6ffc47fb78e8ff11b6da2fcd875f435067f69.jpg)

 Adenot grew up dreaming of flying to space. © Pau Barrena, AFP file photo 

But while logging 3,000 flight hours and 120 combat missions, Adenot never stopped dreaming of space.

She first applied to be a [European Space Agency](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/european-space-agency/) astronaut in 2008 when she was just 25 – but was rejected.

However in 2022 she was selected out of 22,000 candidates, and embarked on three years of intense training to get ready for Friday's launch.

It has been a "tsunami" that has completely changed her life, the mother of a teenager has said.

## Michelin-starred cuisine

Adenot will be busy on board the orbiting scientific lab, participating in more than 200 experiments.

Research will include microgravity's effect on the human body, including measuring how her time in orbit impacts her memory.

She will also test a system that uses artificial intelligence and augmented reality to allow astronauts to carry out their own medical ultrasounds.

But it will not be all work.

French chef Anne-Sophie Pic, who has 10 Michelin stars, has prepared a menu for Adenot that includes lobster bisque and foie gras.

She has also recorded the sounds of birds singing, footsteps crunching on snow and flowing streams to remind her of life back on that blue planet she can see out of the window.

###### Astronaut

# Thomas Pesquet

Thomas Pesquet was born in Rouen, France, on 27 February 1978. He was launched to the International Space Station for his first six-month mission, Proxima, in November 2016. Thomas's second mission to the Space Station, known as Alpha, was from April to November 2021.

###### Biography

### Experience

From April to September 2001, Thomas was a trainee engineer with Thales Alenia Space in Cannes, France, where he developed a satellite system design tool using concurrent engineering techniques.

From October 2001, he worked as a spacecraft dynamics engineer on remote sensing missions for GMV S.A. in Madrid, Spain.

Between 2002 and 2004, Thomas worked at the French space agency, CNES, as a research engineer on space mission autonomy. He also carried out studies on future European ground segment design and European space technology harmonisation. From late 2002, he was a CNES representative at the Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems, working on cross-support between international space agencies.

An avid private pilot in his spare time, Thomas was selected in 2004 for Air France’s flight training programme. He went on to become a commercial pilot for the airline, where he started flying the Airbus A320 in 2006. Having logged more than 2300 flight hours on commercial airliners, he became a type rating instructor on the A320 and a Crew Resource Management instructor.

Thomas was selected as an ESA astronaut in May 2009. He joined ESA in September 2009 and completed basic training in November 2010. After graduation, he worked as a Eurocom, communicating with astronauts during spaceflights from the mission control centre. He was also in charge of future projects at the European Astronaut Centre, including initiating cooperation with new partners such as China.

To be ready for a space mission, he received further technical and operational training in Europe, Russia and the USA: on the Russian Soyuz spacecraft, on the US and Russian spacesuits, and on Space Station systems. He took part in exploration training courses: living and working underground on ESA’s CAVES training course in 2011, and underwater on NASA’s Seatest-2 mission.

On 17 March 2014, Thomas was assigned to his first long-duration mission on the International Space Station. He was launched to the International Space Station for this six-month Proxima mission, as a flight engineer for Expeditions 50 and 51, on 17 November 2016.

Thomas' second spaceflight was announced on 28 July 2020. He traveled to the International Space Station on the second SpaceX Crew Dragon mission together with JAXA astronaut Akihiko Hoshide and NASA astronauts Shane Kimbrough and pilot Megan McArthur. The mission is called Alpha, after Alpha Centauri, the closest stellar system to Earth, following the French tradition to name space missions after stars or constellations. The mission assignment was the first time a European flew to the Space Station in the Crew Dragon, and the first time from USA in over a decade.

When Thomas is not in space or training for his next mission, he enjoys basketball, jogging, swimming, squash and outdoor sports such as mountain biking, kite surfing, sailing, skiing and mountaineering. He also has extensive experience in scuba diving and skydiving and is a black belt in judo. Thomas' other interests include travelling, playing the saxophone and reading.

###### Astronaut

# Thomas Pesquet

Thomas Pesquet was born in Rouen, France, on 27 February 1978. He was launched to the International Space Station for his first six-month mission, Proxima, in November 2016. Thomas's second mission to the Space Station, known as Alpha, was from April to November 2021.

###### Biography

### Experience

From April to September 2001, Thomas was a trainee engineer with Thales Alenia Space in Cannes, France, where he developed a satellite system design tool using concurrent engineering techniques.

From October 2001, he worked as a spacecraft dynamics engineer on remote sensing missions for GMV S.A. in Madrid, Spain.

Between 2002 and 2004, Thomas worked at the French space agency, CNES, as a research engineer on space mission autonomy. He also carried out studies on future European ground segment design and European space technology harmonisation. From late 2002, he was a CNES representative at the Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems, working on cross-support between international space agencies.

An avid private pilot in his spare time, Thomas was selected in 2004 for Air France’s flight training programme. He went on to become a commercial pilot for the airline, where he started flying the Airbus A320 in 2006. Having logged more than 2300 flight hours on commercial airliners, he became a type rating instructor on the A320 and a Crew Resource Management instructor.

Thomas was selected as an ESA astronaut in May 2009. He joined ESA in September 2009 and completed basic training in November 2010. After graduation, he worked as a Eurocom, communicating with astronauts during spaceflights from the mission control centre. He was also in charge of future projects at the European Astronaut Centre, including initiating cooperation with new partners such as China.

To be ready for a space mission, he received further technical and operational training in Europe, Russia and the USA: on the Russian Soyuz spacecraft, on the US and Russian spacesuits, and on Space Station systems. He took part in exploration training courses: living and working underground on ESA’s CAVES training course in 2011, and underwater on NASA’s Seatest-2 mission.

On 17 March 2014, Thomas was assigned to his first long-duration mission on the International Space Station. He was launched to the International Space Station for this six-month Proxima mission, as a flight engineer for Expeditions 50 and 51, on 17 November 2016.

Thomas' second spaceflight was announced on 28 July 2020. He traveled to the International Space Station on the second SpaceX Crew Dragon mission together with JAXA astronaut Akihiko Hoshide and NASA astronauts Shane Kimbrough and pilot Megan McArthur. The mission is called Alpha, after Alpha Centauri, the closest stellar system to Earth, following the French tradition to name space missions after stars or constellations. The mission assignment was the first time a European flew to the Space Station in the Crew Dragon, and the first time from USA in over a decade.

When Thomas is not in space or training for his next mission, he enjoys basketball, jogging, swimming, squash and outdoor sports such as mountain biking, kite surfing, sailing, skiing and mountaineering. He also has extensive experience in scuba diving and skydiving and is a black belt in judo. Thomas' other interests include travelling, playing the saxophone and reading.

###### ESA missions

## 2

Thomas Pesquet is a European Space Agency astronaut of French nationality. He spent six-months on the International Space Station between November 2016 and June 2017 and again between April and November 2021. Thomas served as a flight engineer for Expeditions 50 and 51. He previously worked as an aerospace engineer, and is also an airline pilot for Air France.

France is actively involved in manned space flights. All French cosmonauts have participated in various missions on American and Russian spacecraft. The first French astronaut was Jean-Loup Chretien, who made his first space flight in June 1982 on the Soviet Soyuz T-6 spacecraft.

Jean-Loup Chretien was the first, excluding cosmonauts from the USSR and the USA, to make two space flights, he was also the first French cosmonaut to make a second and third space flight. Chretien became the first cosmonaut from Western Europe. France became the tenth country whose citizen made a space flight. In December 1988, during his flight to the Mir station, Jean-Loup Chretien became the first, excluding cosmonauts of the USSR and the USA, to perform [a spacewalk](https://april12.eu/eva/eva76.html).

Chretien's backup for the flight to Soyuz T-6 was [Patrick Baudry](https://april12.eu/otherastron/baudry172en.html), who became the second French cosmonaut to make a space flight in June 1985 on the American shuttle [Discovery STS-51G](https://april12.eu/sts/discovery/sts51gen.html). Chretien was Baudry's backup.

Four French astronauts have performed spacewalks. Jean-Loup Chretien and Jean-Pierre Haignere performed spacewalks in Russian spacesuits. Philippe Perrin and Thomas Pesquet performed spacewalks in American spacesuits. Thomas Pesquet has performed the most spacewalks among French astronauts - 6 spacewalks with a total duration of 39 hours and 54 minutes.

France, through the European Space Agency, is participating in the International Space Station project. Ten French astronauts have flown into space to date, including one woman, Claudie Andre-Deshaies. Two astronauts made three space flights each.

The longest space flight among French astronauts was made by Thomas Pesquet - 199 days 17 hours 44 minutes (4793 hours 44 minutes). After this flight, Pesquet also became the record holder among French astronauts for the total duration of space flights - 396 days 11 hours 34 minutes 25 seconds (9515 hours 34 minutes 25 seconds).

A total of ten French astronauts made 19 space flights: 9 of them on Russian (USSR) spacecraft «Soyuz», 9 on Space Shuttle and one on the US SpaceX Crew Dragon spacecraft.

Among the French astronauts there is one woman: [Claudie Andre-Deshaies](https://april12.eu/otherastron/andre352en.html) (Enière), who made two space flights on the Russian ships [«Soyuz TM-24»](https://april12.eu/soyuz/soyuztm/syztm24en.html) and [«Soyuz TM-33»](https://april12.eu/soyuz/soyuztm/syztm33en.html).

France is actively involved in manned space flights. All French cosmonauts have participated in various missions on American and Russian spacecraft. The first French astronaut was Jean-Loup Chretien, who made his first space flight in June 1982 on the Soviet Soyuz T-6 spacecraft.

Jean-Loup Chretien was the first, excluding cosmonauts from the USSR and the USA, to make two space flights, he was also the first French cosmonaut to make a second and third space flight. Chretien became the first cosmonaut from Western Europe. France became the tenth country whose citizen made a space flight. In December 1988, during his flight to the Mir station, Jean-Loup Chretien became the first, excluding cosmonauts of the USSR and the USA, to perform [a spacewalk](https://april12.eu/eva/eva76.html).

Chretien's backup for the flight to Soyuz T-6 was [Patrick Baudry](https://april12.eu/otherastron/baudry172en.html), who became the second French cosmonaut to make a space flight in June 1985 on the American shuttle [Discovery STS-51G](https://april12.eu/sts/discovery/sts51gen.html). Chretien was Baudry's backup.

Four French astronauts have performed spacewalks. Jean-Loup Chretien and Jean-Pierre Haignere performed spacewalks in Russian spacesuits. Philippe Perrin and Thomas Pesquet performed spacewalks in American spacesuits. Thomas Pesquet has performed the most spacewalks among French astronauts - 6 spacewalks with a total duration of 39 hours and 54 minutes.

France, through the European Space Agency, is participating in the International Space Station project. Ten French astronauts have flown into space to date, including one woman, Claudie Andre-Deshaies. Two astronauts made three space flights each.

The longest space flight among French astronauts was made by Thomas Pesquet - 199 days 17 hours 44 minutes (4793 hours 44 minutes). After this flight, Pesquet also became the record holder among French astronauts for the total duration of space flights - 396 days 11 hours 34 minutes 25 seconds (9515 hours 34 minutes 25 seconds).

A total of ten French astronauts made 19 space flights: 9 of them on Russian (USSR) spacecraft «Soyuz», 9 on Space Shuttle and one on the US SpaceX Crew Dragon spacecraft.

Among the French astronauts there is one woman: [Claudie Andre-Deshaies](https://april12.eu/otherastron/andre352en.html) (Enière), who made two space flights on the Russian ships [«Soyuz TM-24»](https://april12.eu/soyuz/soyuztm/syztm24en.html) and [«Soyuz TM-33»](https://april12.eu/soyuz/soyuztm/syztm33en.html).

**Sophie Marie Laurence Adenot** (French pronunciation:[[sɔfi ad(ə)no]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French"); born 5 July 1982) is a French engineer, helicopter pilot, and astronaut. She holds the rank of [colonel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonel "Colonel") in the [French Air and Space Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Air_and_Space_Force "French Air and Space Force") and became France's first female helicopter [test pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Test_pilot "Test pilot") in 2018. She was selected to join the [European Astronaut Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Astronaut_Corps "European Astronaut Corps") as part of the [2022 group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_European_Space_Agency_Astronaut_Group "2022 European Space Agency Astronaut Group"). Her first spaceflight began in February 2026 on [SpaceX Crew-12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Crew-12 "SpaceX Crew-12"), during which she launched to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") for a long-duration mission as a part of [Expedition 74](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_74 "Expedition 74")/[75](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_75 "Expedition 75"), where she became the first French woman to conduct a spacewalk.

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sophie_Adenot&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Sophie Marie Laurence[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-lieutenant_promotion-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-2) Adenot was born on 5 July 1982, in [Cosne-Cours-sur-Loire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosne-Cours-sur-Loire "Cosne-Cours-sur-Loire"), [Burgundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burgundy "Burgundy"), France, to pharmacist [Isabelle Adenot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isabelle_Adenot?action=edit&redlink=1 "Isabelle Adenot (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isabelle%20Adenot "fr:Isabelle Adenot")] ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")Alloy) and Hubert Adenot, a notary in [Corbigny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbigny "Corbigny").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-WsW-5) Her mother served as national president of the [French pharmaceutical order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_pharmaceutical_order?action=edit&redlink=1 "French pharmaceutical order (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordre%20national%20des%20pharmaciens "fr:Ordre national des pharmaciens")] from 2009 to 2017.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-7) Childhood inspirations include her grandfather, who served in the [French Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Air_Force "French Air Force") as an [aircraft mechanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_mechanic "Aircraft mechanic"), and the astronaut [Claudie Haigneré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudie_Haigner%C3%A9 "Claudie Haigneré"), who became the first French woman astronaut. She recalled being inspired by watching Haigneré's 1996 launch to the space station _[Mir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mir "Mir")_ live on television.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-8)

Adenot attended a _[maison d'éducation de la Légion d'honneur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maison\_d'%C3%A9ducation\_de\_la\_L%C3%A9gion\_d'honneur "Maison d'éducation de la Légion d'honneur")_ in [Saint-Denis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Denis,_Seine-Saint-Denis "Saint-Denis, Seine-Saint-Denis"), a secondary school open to girls whose father, grandfather or great-grandfather had been awarded the [Legion of Honour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legion_of_Honour "Legion of Honour"), where she obtained her _[baccalauréat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baccalaur%C3%A9at "Baccalauréat")_. She then completed _[classes préparatoires aux grandes écoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classe\_pr%C3%A9paratoire\_aux\_grandes\_%C3%A9coles "Classe préparatoire aux grandes écoles")_ to prepare for entry into a _[grande école](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grande\_%C3%A9cole "Grande école")_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Les%C3%89chos-9)

From 2001 to 2003, she studied engineering at the [Institut Supérieur de l'Aéronautique et de l'Espace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institut_sup%C3%A9rieur_de_l'a%C3%A9ronautique_et_de_l'espace "Institut supérieur de l'aéronautique et de l'espace") (ISAE-SUPAERO), specializing in the [flight dynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_dynamics "Flight dynamics") of aircraft and spacecraft and earned a degree in 2004.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-esa.int_profile-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Ouest-France_23-11-22-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-RFI_2022-12) That same year, she earned a [Master of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Science "Master of Science") in human factors engineering from the [Massachusetts Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Institute_of_Technology "Massachusetts Institute of Technology") (MIT).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Ouest-France_23-11-22-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-RFI_2022-12) While at MIT, she worked in the Man-Vehicle Laboratory and wrote her thesis on how the [vestibular system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vestibular_system "Vestibular system") adapts to [artificial gravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_gravity "Artificial gravity"), contributing to the development of [centrifuge training](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-g_training "High-g training") for astronauts.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-esa.int_profile-10)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sophie_Adenot&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### French Air Force

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sophie_Adenot&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: French Air Force")]

[Video 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/18/Leur_G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ration_%C3%89galit%C3%A9_-_portrait_de_Sophie_Adenot.webm?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

Promotional video produced by the [Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_for_Europe_and_Foreign_Affairs_(France) "Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (France)") (in French)

After graduating, Adenot spent one year working as an engineer at [Airbus Helicopters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbus_Helicopters "Airbus Helicopters") in [Marignane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marignane "Marignane"), focusing on the design of helicopter [cockpits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cockpit "Cockpit"), particularly for the company's [H225](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbus_Helicopters_H225 "Airbus Helicopters H225") model.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Les%C3%89chos-9)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_27-11-2022-13)

Adenot joined the [French Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Air_and_Space_Force "French Air and Space Force") in 2005.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_27-11-2022-13) After completing helicopter pilot training, she was assigned to [Escadron d'Hélicoptères 1/67 Pyrénées](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escadron_d'H%C3%A9licopt%C3%A8res_1/67_Pyr%C3%A9n%C3%A9es "Escadron d'Hélicoptères 1/67 Pyrénées") at [Cazaux Air Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cazaux_Air_Base "Cazaux Air Base"), where she piloted Caracal helicopters on [search and rescue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_and_rescue "Search and rescue") missions in hostile environments from 2008 to 2012.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-esa.int_profile-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_27-11-2022-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-14) In 2008, she applied to the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency "European Space Agency") astronaut programme, the [European Astronaut Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Astronaut_Corps "European Astronaut Corps"), but was rejected.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-France24_13-2-2026-15) She transferred to the High Authority Transport Squadron based in [Villacoublay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villacoublay "Villacoublay"), which is responsible for transporting the head of state, government ministers, and visiting foreign delegations, in 2012.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-esa.int_profile-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_27-11-2022-13)

In 2017, she entered the [école du personnel navigant d'essais et de réception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89cole_du_personnel_navigant_d'essais_et_de_r%C3%A9ception "École du personnel navigant d'essais et de réception"), a test pilot school, and in 2018 became the first female helicopter test pilot in France.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_28-11-2022-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-L'Express_2022-17) After graduating from [Empire Test Pilots' School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_Test_Pilots'_School "Empire Test Pilots' School") in the United Kingdom in 2018, she worked as a helicopter test pilot at Cazaux Air Base under the [French Defence Procurement Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direction_g%C3%A9n%C3%A9rale_de_l'armement "Direction générale de l'armement") from 2019 to 2022.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-esa.int_profile-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_27-11-2022-13)As of 2022[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sophie_Adenot&action=edit), she had accumulated over 3,000 flight hours across 22 different types of helicopters.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-18)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_28-11-2022-16)

Adenot was promoted to the rank of [lieutenant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant "Lieutenant") in August 2006,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-lieutenant_promotion-1)[captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(armed_forces) "Captain (armed forces)") in 2009,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-captain_promotion-19)[commandant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commandant_(rank) "Commandant (rank)") in December 2014,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-commandant_promotion-20)[lieutenant colonel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_colonel "Lieutenant colonel") in June 2020,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-lieutenant_colonel_promotion-21) and [colonel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonel "Colonel") in July 2023.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-colonel_promotion-22)

### European Space Agency

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sophie_Adenot&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: European Space Agency")]

Adenot was selected to join the European Astronaut Corps as part of the [2022 European Space Agency Astronaut Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_European_Space_Agency_Astronaut_Group "2022 European Space Agency Astronaut Group"). She is the second French woman to join the corps, after [Claudie Haigneré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudie_Haigner%C3%A9 "Claudie Haigneré").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-RFI_2022-12)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_28-11-2022-16)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-23) The 2022 class, nicknamed "The Hoppers", was chosen from a pool of 22,500 applicants.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-24)

In 2024, ESA announced that Adenot would be the first member of her class to fly to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") (ISS) for a long-duration mission set for spring 2026.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-26) ESA's portion of the Crew-12 mission—Adenot's assignment—was dubbed "Epsilon".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-27) As part of [SpaceX Crew-12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Crew-12 "SpaceX Crew-12"), Adenot launched to the ISS on 13 February 2026 to join the [Expedition 74](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_74 "Expedition 74") crew.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-France24_13-2-2026-15)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-28) She was set to participate in more than 200 experiments in [microgravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microgravity "Microgravity") during her 8-month stay on the ISS. These experiments include testing a device that allows for autonomous [medical ultrasounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_ultrasound "Medical ultrasound"), named EchoFinder, to determine the impact of [weightlessness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weightlessness "Weightlessness") on herself and other crew members; an experiment, called PhysioTool, to measure several of the body's [physiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiological "Physiological") factors; and an experiment in partnership with French schools, named ChlorISS, to observe the impact of light and gravity on the growth of a _[Arabidopsis thaliana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabidopsis\_thaliana "Arabidopsis thaliana")_ and a _[Brassica rapa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brassica\_rapa "Brassica rapa")_ (_Mizuna_) plant, both from the [mustard family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brassicaceae "Brassicaceae"), and testing a prototype of a space suit, the "[EuroSuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroSuit "EuroSuit")".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-RFI_30-11-2025-29) She also brought a selection of French dishes, including [lobster bisque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lobster_bisque "Lobster bisque") and [foie gras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foie_gras "Foie gras"), created by [Michelin-starred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelin-starred "Michelin-starred") chef [Anne-Sophie Pic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne-Sophie_Pic "Anne-Sophie Pic") to supplement standard onboard meals.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-30)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-France24_13-2-2026-15)

In August 2026, Adenot completed her first [spacewalk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extravehicular_activity "Extravehicular activity").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-31) Alongside NASA astronaut [Anil Menon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Menon "Anil Menon"), she removed a space-to-ground antenna on the station's Z1 truss segment in a spacewalk that lasted about six and a half hours.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-NASA_10-8-2026-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde,_August_2026-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-34) This made Adenot the first French woman, the second European woman after [Samantha Cristoforetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samantha_Cristoforetti "Samantha Cristoforetti") in July 2022 to conduct a spacewalk, and the first to do so wearing an American [Extravehicular Mobility Unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extravehicular_Mobility_Unit "Extravehicular Mobility Unit") (EMU) rather than a Russian [Orlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlan_space_suit "Orlan space suit") suit, which Cristoforetti wore for her spacewalk from the station's [Poisk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisk_(ISS_module) "Poisk (ISS module)") module.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde,_August_2026-33)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-36) In the days before the excursion, Adenot and Menon organized tools inside the station's [Quest Airlock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quest_Joint_Airlock "Quest Joint Airlock"), while commander [Jessica Meir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Meir "Jessica Meir") and flight engineer [Jack Hathaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Hathaway "Jack Hathaway") reviewed the [Canadarm2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadarm2 "Canadarm2") robotic-arm manoeuvres that supported the spacewalkers.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-NASA_10-8-2026-32) Adenot also continued her onboard exercise research, running on the station's [COLBERT treadmill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combined_Operational_Load_Bearing_External_Resistance_Treadmill "Combined Operational Load Bearing External Resistance Treadmill") while wearing the "EasyMotion-2" suit, which delivers electrical impulses to trigger muscle contractions during her workout.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-NASA_10-8-2026-32) Adenot performed a second spacewalk on 25 August, also alongside Menon,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-37) and a third on 1 September alongside Meir.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-38)

## Awards and honours

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sophie_Adenot&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Awards and honours")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/La_Lcl_Sophie_Adenot_d%C3%A9cor%C3%A9e_de_l%27ONM.jpg/250px-La_Lcl_Sophie_Adenot_d%C3%A9cor%C3%A9e_de_l%27ONM.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:La_Lcl_Sophie_Adenot_d%C3%A9cor%C3%A9e_de_l'ONM.jpg)

[French National Order of Merit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordre_national_du_M%C3%A9rite "Ordre national du Mérite") ceremony in 2022

In 2020, Adenot was recognized by the [Young Leaders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French-American_Foundation#Young_Leaders "French-American Foundation") program of the [French-American Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French-American_Foundation "French-American Foundation").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-40)

In 2021, she was awarded the [Medal of the French National Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9daille_de_l'Assembl%C3%A9e_nationale?action=edit&redlink=1 "Médaille de l'Assemblée nationale (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9daille%20de%20l'Assembl%C3%A9e%20nationale "fr:Médaille de l'Assemblée nationale")] for her "actions as an inspiring ambassador for gender equality in sciences".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-esa.int_profile-10) She was appointed a _chevalier_ of the [French National Order of Merit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordre_national_du_M%C3%A9rite "Ordre national du Mérite") in 2022.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Ouest-France_23-11-22-11) She is a recipient of the country's [Aeronautical Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeronautical_Medal "Aeronautical Medal").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-41)

She was appointed a _chevalier_ of the [National Order of the Legion of Honour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Order_of_the_Legion_of_Honour "National Order of the Legion of Honour") on 14 July 2026.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-42)

**Sophie Marie Laurence Adenot** (French pronunciation:[[sɔfi ad(ə)no]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French"); born 5 July 1982) is a French engineer, helicopter pilot, and astronaut. She holds the rank of [colonel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonel "Colonel") in the [French Air and Space Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Air_and_Space_Force "French Air and Space Force") and became France's first female helicopter [test pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Test_pilot "Test pilot") in 2018. She was selected to join the [European Astronaut Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Astronaut_Corps "European Astronaut Corps") as part of the [2022 group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_European_Space_Agency_Astronaut_Group "2022 European Space Agency Astronaut Group"). Her first spaceflight began in February 2026 on [SpaceX Crew-12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Crew-12 "SpaceX Crew-12"), during which she launched to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") for a long-duration mission as a part of [Expedition 74](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_74 "Expedition 74")/[75](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_75 "Expedition 75"), where she became the first French woman to conduct a spacewalk.

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sophie_Adenot&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Sophie Marie Laurence[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-lieutenant_promotion-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-2) Adenot was born on 5 July 1982, in [Cosne-Cours-sur-Loire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosne-Cours-sur-Loire "Cosne-Cours-sur-Loire"), [Burgundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burgundy "Burgundy"), France, to pharmacist [Isabelle Adenot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isabelle_Adenot?action=edit&redlink=1 "Isabelle Adenot (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isabelle%20Adenot "fr:Isabelle Adenot")] ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")Alloy) and Hubert Adenot, a notary in [Corbigny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbigny "Corbigny").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-WsW-5) Her mother served as national president of the [French pharmaceutical order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_pharmaceutical_order?action=edit&redlink=1 "French pharmaceutical order (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordre%20national%20des%20pharmaciens "fr:Ordre national des pharmaciens")] from 2009 to 2017.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-7) Childhood inspirations include her grandfather, who served in the [French Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Air_Force "French Air Force") as an [aircraft mechanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_mechanic "Aircraft mechanic"), and the astronaut [Claudie Haigneré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudie_Haigner%C3%A9 "Claudie Haigneré"), who became the first French woman astronaut. She recalled being inspired by watching Haigneré's 1996 launch to the space station _[Mir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mir "Mir")_ live on television.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-8)

Adenot attended a _[maison d'éducation de la Légion d'honneur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maison\_d'%C3%A9ducation\_de\_la\_L%C3%A9gion\_d'honneur "Maison d'éducation de la Légion d'honneur")_ in [Saint-Denis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Denis,_Seine-Saint-Denis "Saint-Denis, Seine-Saint-Denis"), a secondary school open to girls whose father, grandfather or great-grandfather had been awarded the [Legion of Honour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legion_of_Honour "Legion of Honour"), where she obtained her _[baccalauréat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baccalaur%C3%A9at "Baccalauréat")_. She then completed _[classes préparatoires aux grandes écoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classe\_pr%C3%A9paratoire\_aux\_grandes\_%C3%A9coles "Classe préparatoire aux grandes écoles")_ to prepare for entry into a _[grande école](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grande\_%C3%A9cole "Grande école")_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Les%C3%89chos-9)

From 2001 to 2003, she studied engineering at the [Institut Supérieur de l'Aéronautique et de l'Espace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institut_sup%C3%A9rieur_de_l'a%C3%A9ronautique_et_de_l'espace "Institut supérieur de l'aéronautique et de l'espace") (ISAE-SUPAERO), specializing in the [flight dynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_dynamics "Flight dynamics") of aircraft and spacecraft and earned a degree in 2004.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-esa.int_profile-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Ouest-France_23-11-22-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-RFI_2022-12) That same year, she earned a [Master of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Science "Master of Science") in human factors engineering from the [Massachusetts Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Institute_of_Technology "Massachusetts Institute of Technology") (MIT).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Ouest-France_23-11-22-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-RFI_2022-12) While at MIT, she worked in the Man-Vehicle Laboratory and wrote her thesis on how the [vestibular system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vestibular_system "Vestibular system") adapts to [artificial gravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_gravity "Artificial gravity"), contributing to the development of [centrifuge training](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-g_training "High-g training") for astronauts.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-esa.int_profile-10)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sophie_Adenot&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### French Air Force

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sophie_Adenot&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: French Air Force")]

[Video 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/18/Leur_G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ration_%C3%89galit%C3%A9_-_portrait_de_Sophie_Adenot.webm?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

Promotional video produced by the [Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_for_Europe_and_Foreign_Affairs_(France) "Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (France)") (in French)

After graduating, Adenot spent one year working as an engineer at [Airbus Helicopters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbus_Helicopters "Airbus Helicopters") in [Marignane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marignane "Marignane"), focusing on the design of helicopter [cockpits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cockpit "Cockpit"), particularly for the company's [H225](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbus_Helicopters_H225 "Airbus Helicopters H225") model.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Les%C3%89chos-9)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_27-11-2022-13)

Adenot joined the [French Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Air_and_Space_Force "French Air and Space Force") in 2005.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_27-11-2022-13) After completing helicopter pilot training, she was assigned to [Escadron d'Hélicoptères 1/67 Pyrénées](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escadron_d'H%C3%A9licopt%C3%A8res_1/67_Pyr%C3%A9n%C3%A9es "Escadron d'Hélicoptères 1/67 Pyrénées") at [Cazaux Air Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cazaux_Air_Base "Cazaux Air Base"), where she piloted Caracal helicopters on [search and rescue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_and_rescue "Search and rescue") missions in hostile environments from 2008 to 2012.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-esa.int_profile-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_27-11-2022-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-14) In 2008, she applied to the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency "European Space Agency") astronaut programme, the [European Astronaut Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Astronaut_Corps "European Astronaut Corps"), but was rejected.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-France24_13-2-2026-15) She transferred to the High Authority Transport Squadron based in [Villacoublay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villacoublay "Villacoublay"), which is responsible for transporting the head of state, government ministers, and visiting foreign delegations, in 2012.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-esa.int_profile-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_27-11-2022-13)

In 2017, she entered the [école du personnel navigant d'essais et de réception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89cole_du_personnel_navigant_d'essais_et_de_r%C3%A9ception "École du personnel navigant d'essais et de réception"), a test pilot school, and in 2018 became the first female helicopter test pilot in France.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_28-11-2022-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-L'Express_2022-17) After graduating from [Empire Test Pilots' School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_Test_Pilots'_School "Empire Test Pilots' School") in the United Kingdom in 2018, she worked as a helicopter test pilot at Cazaux Air Base under the [French Defence Procurement Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direction_g%C3%A9n%C3%A9rale_de_l'armement "Direction générale de l'armement") from 2019 to 2022.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-esa.int_profile-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_27-11-2022-13)As of 2022[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sophie_Adenot&action=edit), she had accumulated over 3,000 flight hours across 22 different types of helicopters.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-18)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_28-11-2022-16)

Adenot was promoted to the rank of [lieutenant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant "Lieutenant") in August 2006,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-lieutenant_promotion-1)[captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(armed_forces) "Captain (armed forces)") in 2009,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-captain_promotion-19)[commandant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commandant_(rank) "Commandant (rank)") in December 2014,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-commandant_promotion-20)[lieutenant colonel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_colonel "Lieutenant colonel") in June 2020,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-lieutenant_colonel_promotion-21) and [colonel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonel "Colonel") in July 2023.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-colonel_promotion-22)

### European Space Agency

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sophie_Adenot&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: European Space Agency")]

Adenot was selected to join the European Astronaut Corps as part of the [2022 European Space Agency Astronaut Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_European_Space_Agency_Astronaut_Group "2022 European Space Agency Astronaut Group"). She is the second French woman to join the corps, after [Claudie Haigneré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudie_Haigner%C3%A9 "Claudie Haigneré").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-RFI_2022-12)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde_28-11-2022-16)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-23) The 2022 class, nicknamed "The Hoppers", was chosen from a pool of 22,500 applicants.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-24)

In 2024, ESA announced that Adenot would be the first member of her class to fly to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") (ISS) for a long-duration mission set for spring 2026.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-26) ESA's portion of the Crew-12 mission—Adenot's assignment—was dubbed "Epsilon".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-27) As part of [SpaceX Crew-12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Crew-12 "SpaceX Crew-12"), Adenot launched to the ISS on 13 February 2026 to join the [Expedition 74](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_74 "Expedition 74") crew.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-France24_13-2-2026-15)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-28) She was set to participate in more than 200 experiments in [microgravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microgravity "Microgravity") during her 8-month stay on the ISS. These experiments include testing a device that allows for autonomous [medical ultrasounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_ultrasound "Medical ultrasound"), named EchoFinder, to determine the impact of [weightlessness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weightlessness "Weightlessness") on herself and other crew members; an experiment, called PhysioTool, to measure several of the body's [physiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiological "Physiological") factors; and an experiment in partnership with French schools, named ChlorISS, to observe the impact of light and gravity on the growth of a _[Arabidopsis thaliana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabidopsis\_thaliana "Arabidopsis thaliana")_ and a _[Brassica rapa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brassica\_rapa "Brassica rapa")_ (_Mizuna_) plant, both from the [mustard family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brassicaceae "Brassicaceae"), and testing a prototype of a space suit, the "[EuroSuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroSuit "EuroSuit")".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-RFI_30-11-2025-29) She also brought a selection of French dishes, including [lobster bisque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lobster_bisque "Lobster bisque") and [foie gras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foie_gras "Foie gras"), created by [Michelin-starred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelin-starred "Michelin-starred") chef [Anne-Sophie Pic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne-Sophie_Pic "Anne-Sophie Pic") to supplement standard onboard meals.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-30)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-France24_13-2-2026-15)

In August 2026, Adenot completed her first [spacewalk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extravehicular_activity "Extravehicular activity").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-31) Alongside NASA astronaut [Anil Menon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Menon "Anil Menon"), she removed a space-to-ground antenna on the station's Z1 truss segment in a spacewalk that lasted about six and a half hours.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-NASA_10-8-2026-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde,_August_2026-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-34) This made Adenot the first French woman, the second European woman after [Samantha Cristoforetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samantha_Cristoforetti "Samantha Cristoforetti") in July 2022 to conduct a spacewalk, and the first to do so wearing an American [Extravehicular Mobility Unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extravehicular_Mobility_Unit "Extravehicular Mobility Unit") (EMU) rather than a Russian [Orlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlan_space_suit "Orlan space suit") suit, which Cristoforetti wore for her spacewalk from the station's [Poisk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisk_(ISS_module) "Poisk (ISS module)") module.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-Le_Monde,_August_2026-33)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-36) In the days before the excursion, Adenot and Menon organized tools inside the station's [Quest Airlock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quest_Joint_Airlock "Quest Joint Airlock"), while commander [Jessica Meir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Meir "Jessica Meir") and flight engineer [Jack Hathaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Hathaway "Jack Hathaway") reviewed the [Canadarm2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadarm2 "Canadarm2") robotic-arm manoeuvres that supported the spacewalkers.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-NASA_10-8-2026-32) Adenot also continued her onboard exercise research, running on the station's [COLBERT treadmill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combined_Operational_Load_Bearing_External_Resistance_Treadmill "Combined Operational Load Bearing External Resistance Treadmill") while wearing the "EasyMotion-2" suit, which delivers electrical impulses to trigger muscle contractions during her workout.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-NASA_10-8-2026-32) Adenot performed a second spacewalk on 25 August, also alongside Menon,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-37) and a third on 1 September alongside Meir.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Adenot#cite_note-38)

# France's second woman in space prepares for launch after 30-year wait

French astronaut Sophie Adenot is set to fly to the International Space Station on Friday, 13 February 2026. She will launch at around 11:00 CET from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida as part of NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission. The launch was due to take place today, Thursday, but was postponed because of bad weather. They are due to dock with ISS on Saturday evening.

The crew will launch aboard a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft on a Falcon 9 rocket. Adenot will be joined by NASA astronauts Jessica Meir (mission commander), Jack Hathaway (pilot), and Russian cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev (mission specialist).

[Who is Sophie Adenot, the French engineer destined for space?](https://www.rfi.fr/en/science-and-technology/20221124-who-is-sophie-adenot-the-french-engineer-destined-for-space-astronaut)

Adenot, 43, holds the rank of colonel in the French Air and [Space](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/space/) Force. She will become only the second Frenchwoman in space in more than 30 years, following Claudie Haigneré's historic missions in the 1990s and early 2000s.

[France's first woman in space in 25 years counts down to trip to the ISS](https://www.rfi.fr/en/science-and-technology/20251130-france-first-woman-in-space-in-25-years-prepares-for-trip-to-the-iss-sophie-adenot)

Haigneré first flew to space in August 1996 aboard Soyuz TM-24, spending 16 days on the Russian space station Mir during the Cassiopée mission. In October 2001, she became the first European woman to visit the International Space Station during the Andromède mission.

The Crew-12 mission will be Adenot's first spaceflight. The [European Space Agency](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/european-space-agency/) has named her mission εpsilon (Epsilon). Selected as an ESA astronaut in November 2022 from a pool of 22,500 applicants, she became the first member of her class to receive a flight assignment.

Adenot earned an engineering degree from ISAE-SUPAERO in Toulouse, France, specialising in spacecraft and aircraft flight dynamics. She also holds a master's degree in human factors engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the [United States](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/united-states/).

[France's Sophie Adenot to spend nine months on ISS after medical evacuation](https://www.rfi.fr/en/science-and-technology/20260115-france-sophie-adenot-to-spend-nine-months-on-iss-after-medical-evacuation)

Before joining ESA, she became France's first female helicopter test pilot in 2018, accumulating over 3,000 flight hours on 22 different types of helicopter.

**Adenot's experiments**

Josef Aschbacher, Director General of the European Space Agency, said Adenot's mission is very important for Europe as she will be conducting experiments during her six-to-eight-month stay on the [International](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/international/) Space Station.

The aim is to develop space science and technology through these experiments. This forms a vital part of exploration work and is crucial for developing expertise in space, Aschbacher told [RFI English](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/rfi-english/) following his press briefing in January.

According to CNES, [France](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/france/)'s space agency, Adenot will contribute to approximately 200 experiments during her stay. Seven have been specifically prepared for the Epsilon mission by CADMOS, CNES's centre for the development of microgravity applications and space operations in Toulouse.

[ESA at 50: looking back and launching forward](https://www.rfi.fr/en/science-and-technology/20250609-esa-at-50-looking-back-and-launching-forward)

The experiments will focus on physiology, technology testing for future Moon and Mars missions, and educational outreach.

The mission name, Epsilon, is the fifth Greek letter and follows the French tradition of naming human spaceflight missions after celestial bodies.

# France's second woman in space prepares for launch after 30-year wait

French astronaut Sophie Adenot is set to fly to the International Space Station on Friday, 13 February 2026. She will launch at around 11:00 CET from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida as part of NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission. The launch was due to take place today, Thursday, but was postponed because of bad weather. They are due to dock with ISS on Saturday evening.

The crew will launch aboard a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft on a Falcon 9 rocket. Adenot will be joined by NASA astronauts Jessica Meir (mission commander), Jack Hathaway (pilot), and Russian cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev (mission specialist).

[Who is Sophie Adenot, the French engineer destined for space?](https://www.rfi.fr/en/science-and-technology/20221124-who-is-sophie-adenot-the-french-engineer-destined-for-space-astronaut)

Adenot, 43, holds the rank of colonel in the French Air and [Space](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/space/) Force. She will become only the second Frenchwoman in space in more than 30 years, following Claudie Haigneré's historic missions in the 1990s and early 2000s.

[France's first woman in space in 25 years counts down to trip to the ISS](https://www.rfi.fr/en/science-and-technology/20251130-france-first-woman-in-space-in-25-years-prepares-for-trip-to-the-iss-sophie-adenot)

Haigneré first flew to space in August 1996 aboard Soyuz TM-24, spending 16 days on the Russian space station Mir during the Cassiopée mission. In October 2001, she became the first European woman to visit the International Space Station during the Andromède mission.

The Crew-12 mission will be Adenot's first spaceflight. The [European Space Agency](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/european-space-agency/) has named her mission εpsilon (Epsilon). Selected as an ESA astronaut in November 2022 from a pool of 22,500 applicants, she became the first member of her class to receive a flight assignment.

Adenot earned an engineering degree from ISAE-SUPAERO in Toulouse, France, specialising in spacecraft and aircraft flight dynamics. She also holds a master's degree in human factors engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the [United States](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/united-states/).

[France's Sophie Adenot to spend nine months on ISS after medical evacuation](https://www.rfi.fr/en/science-and-technology/20260115-france-sophie-adenot-to-spend-nine-months-on-iss-after-medical-evacuation)

Before joining ESA, she became France's first female helicopter test pilot in 2018, accumulating over 3,000 flight hours on 22 different types of helicopter.

**Adenot's experiments**

Josef Aschbacher, Director General of the European Space Agency, said Adenot's mission is very important for Europe as she will be conducting experiments during her six-to-eight-month stay on the [International](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/international/) Space Station.

The aim is to develop space science and technology through these experiments. This forms a vital part of exploration work and is crucial for developing expertise in space, Aschbacher told [RFI English](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/rfi-english/) following his press briefing in January.

According to CNES, [France](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/france/)'s space agency, Adenot will contribute to approximately 200 experiments during her stay. Seven have been specifically prepared for the Epsilon mission by CADMOS, CNES's centre for the development of microgravity applications and space operations in Toulouse.

[ESA at 50: looking back and launching forward](https://www.rfi.fr/en/science-and-technology/20250609-esa-at-50-looking-back-and-launching-forward)

The experiments will focus on physiology, technology testing for future Moon and Mars missions, and educational outreach.

The mission name, Epsilon, is the fifth Greek letter and follows the French tradition of naming human spaceflight missions after celestial bodies.

**Jean-Loup Jacques Marie Chrétien** (born 20 August 1938) is a French retired _Général de Brigade_ (brigadier general) in the _[Armée de l'Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French\_Air\_and\_Space\_Force "French Air and Space Force")_ (French air force), and a former [CNES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNES "CNES")[spationaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut"). He flew on two Franco-Soviet space missions and a [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA")[Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle") mission. Chrétien was the first Frenchman and the first western European in space.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jean-Loup_Chr%C3%A9tien&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Chrétien was born in the town of [La Rochelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Rochelle "La Rochelle"), France. He was married to and then divorced from Amy Kristine Jensen of [New Canaan, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Canaan,_Connecticut "New Canaan, Connecticut"), and had five children. His father, Jacques, was a Navy sailor, and his mother, the former Marie-Blanche Coudurier, was a housewife. Chrétien is fluent in French, English and Russian.

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jean-Loup_Chr%C3%A9tien&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Education")]

Chrétien was educated at the École communale in [Ploujean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ploujean "Ploujean"), the Collège Saint-Charles in [Saint-Brieuc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Brieuc "Saint-Brieuc"), and the Lycée de [Morlaix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morlaix "Morlaix"). He entered the [École de l'Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89cole_de_l'air_et_de_l'espace "École de l'air et de l'espace") (the French Air Force Academy) at [Salon-de-Provence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salon-de-Provence "Salon-de-Provence") and graduated in 1961, receiving a master's degree in aeronautical engineering.
